title: Joint tuning of KV quantization and expert residency - contract and fixtures

checkpoint_revision.note: same checkpoint for every comparison (plan contract)

kv_bytes_per_token_fp8.note: derived, not independently measured; treat as approximate until phase b

invariants: Same checkpoint for every comparison (byte-identical config/HF quant digests).

Two comparisons only: (A) same expert slots -> isolates the KV codec restore/read effect; (B) same VRAM budget -> captures the system tradeoff (smaller KV frees slots -> fewer expert misses). A codec win must be attributed by A, not inferred from B.
Byte/scale accounting is exact: packed codes + E4M3 block scales + fp32 row scales per the codec table; page/index maps and counters exact.
Unsupported codecs fail loudly at pool construction (ValueError/NotImplementedError); never silently serve a 16-bit slab priced as packed.
nvfp4 requires paged FULL / hybrid-SWA / QSA groups with head_dim % 16 == 0.
No cache size from a negative remaining budget (memory contract); RAM reserve respected.
Null measurement is not zero: OOM/error rows are reported separately, never averaged in.

cases.given: each codec (bf16/fp8/nvfp4) and the supported pools

cases.expected: decode tok/s and PPL at identical slots -> isolates codec restore
different slot counts and miss rates -> captures system tradeoff
cases.assertion: record slots, miss, tok/s per codec

cases.expected: ValueError / NotImplementedError, not a silent downgrade

cases.given: a group with head_dim not divisible by 16
fp8 appears faster than bf16 at high context
cases.expected: if the gain vanishes at same slots it is residency, not the codec
cases.assertion: report both A and B; never attribute a B gain to the codec

cases.expected: quant overhead may make decode slower; no adoption claim at low context from a high-context win

cases.given: DSA/MLA or DSV4/BSA pool with a quant codec

argv: quant or nvfp4 or fp8 or codec or reject
commands.note: baseline before any code edit: 20 passed, 4 skipped

performance_gate.metric: median output tok/s (paired, uninstrumented) and expert miss rate
performance_gate.threshold: >=5% vs prod (nvfp4, manual 2600) at 16k/64k while keeping 220k, or an equal-throughput capacity gain with no miss regression
performance_gate.guard: byte tests exact; no silent dtype downgrade; per-context reporting

quality_gate.ppl: record codec delta vs bf16 (nvfp4 +0.87%, fp8 +0.23% per prod measurement); do not regress beyond the KV epic gate
quality_gate.attribution: same-slot comparison decides codec quality/speed; same-VRAM comparison only decides the system tradeoff

rollback_recipe: Prod keeps --kv-cache-dtype nvfp4; restore by reverting any pool/codec source edit (git checkout scope_files) and by setting the systemd drop-in back to nvfp4. Byte tests (18a-CMD1/2) must pass before and after.
limitations: fp8 bytes/token is derived from the 07 capacity ratio, not independently measured; phase b should confirm.
bf16 KV at 220k needs 5.56 GiB and may not fit alongside the expert cache; bf16 rows at 220k are expected to OOM and are reported, not averaged.
Only MHA/hybrid-SWA/QSA have quant scale-read paths in this tree; MLA is 5y2.18 backlog.
Heap: --moe-cache-auto resolution is shared with task 07/45; this task must not relitigate the 220k-vs-32k tradeoff.
